Wires up the backend consent/hospital/patient APIs into the React frontend. Existing pages had inline fetch calls; the consent detail modal was missing the fetch-record step; and patients had no UI to approve or reject consent requests.

New page at `/patient/consent` where patients see all consent requests targeting their records and can approve or reject:
```js
PATCH /api/v1/consent/{id}/patient-decision/  →  { patient_choice: 'APPROVED' | 'REJECTED' }
```

body:
## The smoking gun

Your diagnostic log:

```
First captured race_position=P1 (current_race_time=123.75s)
Position changed P1→P13 (current_race_time=0.02s, samples=577)
```

Forza ticks `current_race_time` UP during the entire pre-race countdown (broadcasting phantom `race_position=1` the whole time), then **resets it to ~0 the instant the race actually begins**. The position at that reset packet is the real grid slot (P13 in your case).

The mode-of-60 heuristic from #38 landed on P1 because countdown is much longer than 1 second of capture — phantom dominated the first 60 packets.

## Fix

`Session` tracks `_last_crt` and `_grid_pos_at_start`. On every packet, if `current_race_time` decreased sharply (from >1.0s down to <0.5s), we just hit the race-start moment — capture that packet's race_position as the real grid.

`update_state` and `Session.close` prefer `_grid_pos_at_start` when set; fall back to the mode-of-history helper for sessions where Forza didn't show a clear reset (rare, but defensive).

## Verified

Inline assertion replays your exact log scenario:
- 5 phantom P1 packets during 124s countdown → no grid set yet ✓
- Reset packet (crt 123.75→0.02, position 13) → `_grid_pos_at_start = 13` ✓
- Mid-race progression to P8 → finish = 8 (latest), grid stays 13 ✓

After your next AI race:

```
grep 'Race start detected' listener.log | tail
```

Should show `grid=PN` where N is your actual starting position.

Adds optional Kubernetes-native `Ingress` support to each of the five services in `istari-platform` (frontend, fileservice, mcp, secure-connection, docs). Default-off; opt in per service via `{service}.ingress.enabled: true`. Customers without Istio currently have to manage routing resources out-of-band. The immediate driver is on-demand per-PR `frontend` instances on isolated subdomains; the general capability is opt-in north-south routing for any service the chart deploys.

## Summary

This PR implements the complete v1.0 MVP of Cost Engine, a Decimal-based process cost calculation engine. It includes the core calculation engine (material, process, energy, overhead), three input adapters (YAML, Excel, ERP CSV), a CLI interface, master data snapshot management, and audit/reproducibility infrastructure.

## Key Changes

### Core Calculation Engine (Phase 02)
- **`src/cost_engine/core/`**: Foundational types and data structures
  - `types.py`: Decimal-backed semantic types (`Money`, `Quantity`, `Yield`, `AllocationRate`) with validation
  - `breakdown.py`: `CostBreakdown`, `CreditLine`, `CostResult` containers with credit line support
  - `units.py`: Unit enums (mass, time, energy) and conversion helpers per units-conventions.md

- **`src/cost_engine/costing/`**: Four-component cost calculation
  - `material.py`: Material cost formula `C_mat = Σ(q_i × p_i) / y`
  - `process.py`: Process cost formula `C_proc = Σ(t_j × r_j)` (direct labor only)
  - `energy.py`: Energy cost formula `C_energy = Σ(u × e)`
  - `overhead.py` + `allocation.py`: Overhead pool calculation and multi-pool allocation with sum-conservation invariant

- **`src/cost_engine/calc.py`**: Top-level `compute_unit_cost()` integration function that stitches all four components

### Input Adapters (Phase 03)
- **`src/cost_engine/io/`**: Unified input parsing framework
  - `adapter.py`: Abstract `InputAdapter` base class and `CostEngineInputs` DTO
  - `errors.py` + `validation.py`: Shared validation framework with `ValidationIssue` and `ValidationError`
  - `yaml_adapter.py`: YAML/dict input parser (MVP primary user input path)
  - `excel_adapter.py`: Excel workbook parser with multi-sheet layout support
  - `erp_adapter.py`: ERP CSV master data parser (items, process rates, utility rates, overhead rates)
  - `schema.py` + `excel_layout.py`: Schema definitions for each format

### Master Data & Snapshots (Phase 04)
- **`src/cost_engine/masters/`**: Master data versioning and integrity
  - `snapshot.py`: `MasterSnapshot` with SHA-256 per-file integrity and `SnapshotStore` for versioned storage
  - `diff.py`: `SnapshotDiff` and `render_diff()` for change tracking between snapshots
  - `expiry.py`: TTL-based expiry detection with `ExpiryPolicy` and `ExpiryStatus`

### CLI & Reporting (Phase 05)
- **`src/cost_engine/cli/`**: Command-line interface
  - `main.py`: Entry point with `calc`, `merge`, `snapshot` subcommands; auto-detects input format
  - `report.py`: Markdown and text report renderers for cost breakdowns

### Analysis Tools (Phase 06)
- **`src/cost_engine/analysis/`**: Sensitivity and scenario analysis
  - `sensitivity.py`: Single-variable sweep engine with `sweep()` function
  - `scenario.py`: Multi-scenario comparison with `compare_scenarios()`
  - `report.py`: Table renderers for sensitivity and scenario results

### Audit & Reproducibility (Phase 07)
- **`src/cost_engine/audit/`**: Calculation traceability
  - `repro.py`: `ReproBundle` with SHA-256 hashing of inputs, results, and master snapshots
  - `log.py`: Append-only JSONL audit log with per-entry integrity (`AuditLog`, `AuditLogEntry`)
  - `outliers.py`: Outlier detection rules (`RangeBoundRule`, `RelativeDeviationRule`)

author: mgwirtzr
body:
1. Problem Statement
The application contained a race condition where a POST /publish request could return a stale version of a draft if a POST /draft request was still "in flight" (simulated by a commit delay). Because the server did not ensure that the save operation was complete before the publish operation read the state, users could inadvertently publish old content.

2. Evidence (The Trace)
I added high-resolution instrumentation to the server and developed a deterministic test harness in harness/race_test.js.

As documented in the attached trace.txt, I observed the following sequence:

POST /draft (Version B) enters the handler.

POST /publish enters the handler while the draft is still awaiting its commit timeout.

POST /publish exits, returning the old content ("Version A").

POST /draft finally completes its commit.

3. The Fix: Serialized Promise Gate
I implemented a Serialized Promise Gate in app/server.js.

Mechanism: I introduced a global draftCommitGate promise chain. Each POST /draft request appends its completion to this chain.

Synchronization: The POST /publish handler now awaits the draftCommitGate before reading the currentDraft state. This ensures that the publish action is "queued" behind any pending saves.

Verification: After applying this fix, both the provided regression tests (npm test) and the manual harness (npm run harness:race) pass successfully. The instrumentation now shows the publish handler waiting for the save to exit before proceeding.

4. Critical Review & Limitations
I conducted a critical review of this implementation with a Senior Engineer (AI). The full review and my reflections are documented in review.md.

Key Takeaways from the Review:

Scope: The fix is effective for the single-process, memory-based state of this assignment.

Limitations: The current Promise gate does not have a timeout, meaning a save could block all future publishes. Additionally, while it serializes the barrier for the publish handler, it does not fully serialize the underlying writes (a "write-after-write" hazard could still exist under variable latency).

Future Improvements: For a production system, I would recommend database-level transactions or a versioned document store to ensure durability and stronger consistency.

5. Files Added/Modified:
app/server.js: Added instrumentation and the Promise gate fix.

harness/race_test.js: Deterministic test harness.

trace.txt: Log evidence of the original race condition.

review.md: Critical AI review and developer reflection.

ai-conversation-fix.md: Record of the AI interaction for the fix.

## Summary

Fixes #1012. Typing a Chinese word (Pinyin or Rime) in the SQL editor scrolled to the end of the script after committing the candidate. Same shape happens for any IME-backed input: option-e then é, Japanese kana, etc.

`TextView.insertText(_:replacementRange:)` was doing **two** edits per IME commit:

1. `unmarkText()` → `replaceCharacters(in: markedRanges, with: "")` to wipe the marked text.
2. `_insertText` → `replaceCharacters(in: replacementRange, with: "测试")` with the same range AppKit had supplied at commit time.

By the time edit #2 ran, the document had shrunk by `markedRanges.totalLength`. The range AppKit gave us pointed at characters that no longer existed:

- **Mid-document marked text** → edit #2 ate whatever happened to follow the wiped marked range. Test `imeCommitInTheMiddleDoesNotCorruptText` reproduces: typed marked "ceshi" at offset 6 of "alpha\\n\\nbeta" then committed "测试" → `string` came out as `"alpha\\n测试"` instead of `"alpha\\n测试\\nbeta"` (the `\\nbeta` portion was eaten).
- **End-of-document marked text** → edit #2's range was out of bounds; `TextStory` raised `Range invalid for string`. The test runner caught it as a fatal error. In the released app the failure mode is "cursor lands at `documentLength`, scroll jumps there" — same root cause.

`insertText` now resolves the effective range(s) **before** clearing marked-text bookkeeping and performs **one** `replaceCharacters` call. Multi-cursor IME (where each cursor gets its own marked range) replaces every range in one pass.

## Latent bug exposed by the fix

`TextSelectionManager.didReplaceCharacters` had the wrong `delta` formula:

\`\`\`swift
let delta = replacementLength == 0 ? -range.length : replacementLength   // before
let delta = replacementLength - range.length                              // after
\`\`\`

Selections at offsets past `range.max` shift by `delta`. The old formula dropped the chars-removed term, so a same-length replace (e.g. "´" → "é" in the multi-cursor IME path) over-shifted later selections by `range.length`. The unmark-then-insert flow happened to mask this because all of its replaces had `replacementLength == 0`. With the single-edit IME path, the bug surfaced and broke the existing `test_markedTextMultipleSelection`. Same-length replaces now leave selections past the replace point unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] New `IMEInputTests` — 5 cases covering middle-of-doc commit, end-of-doc commit, NSNotFound replacement range, marked-state cleanup, and the plain Latin path. All fail on \`main\`; all pass on this branch.
- [x] All 6 existing `MarkedTextTests` (multi-cursor IME) still pass.
- [x] Full \`swift test\` suite: 81 swift-testing + 44 XCTest, all green.
- [x] \`xcodebuild ... build\` succeeds.
- [x] \`swiftlint --strict\` clean on all touched files.
- [ ] Manual on the test fixture: open a SQL script, place caret on a blank line in the middle, type "ceshi" via Pinyin, press space to commit "测试". Caret stays at the inserted text; scroll position stays put.

## Summary

Adds an MVP OpenTelemetry tracing layer to the gateway. Disabled by default; when enabled, the process exports spans over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf) to a configurable collector endpoint. W3C trace-context propagation continues distributed traces from upstream callers.

- New module `src/observability/` wires `tracing-opentelemetry` + `opentelemetry-otlp` (HTTP/protobuf) into the existing fmt subscriber.
- Axum middleware emits a `Received Proxy Server Request` span per inbound request; routes (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`) emit child `llm_request` / `llm_messages` spans per upstream provider call (one per failover attempt).
- Config schema gains `observability.otel { enabled, exporter, endpoint, service_name, headers }`. All call-sites that build `AppConfig` (tests + setup) updated.
- Standard OTel env vars and Rausu-prefixed equivalents both override the YAML config (`RAUSU_OTEL_ENABLED`, `RAUSU_OTEL_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, etc.).

## Privacy

Spans intentionally carry **only safe metadata**: HTTP method, route, status code, provider name, request model, `is_stream` flag, and span timing. The implementation never records:

- request or response bodies
- system prompts, user content, or tool-call arguments
- API keys, OAuth tokens, or any header secrets

This contract is documented in `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` and `docs/OBSERVABILITY_CN.md`, and reinforced in module-level docs on `src/observability/mod.rs`.

## How to enable

```yaml
observability:
  otel:
    enabled: true
    exporter: otlp_http
    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4318/v1/traces\"
    service_name: rausu
```

Or via env:

```bash
RAUSU_OTEL_ENABLED=true RAUSU_OTEL_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318/v1/traces cargo run
```

See `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` for the full configuration reference, env-var matrix, and a quickstart pointing at a local OTel Collector.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- [x] `cargo test` — 506/506 passed (379 unit + 127 integration, including new `tests/observability_test.rs`)
- [ ] Manual smoke against a local OpenTelemetry Collector (`docker run otel/opentelemetry-collector`) — recommended before merge
- [ ] Verify `traceparent` propagation from an instrumented client continues into Rausu spans

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this MVP)

- Optional OTLP/gRPC exporter (only HTTP/protobuf is wired today)
- Live integration test against an embedded collector (currently documented as opt-in only)
- Metrics + logs pipelines (this PR is traces only)
- Per-route attribute enrichment (e.g. usage tokens, finish reason) — keeping the surface small for the MVP

body:
# PR-A: Catch deploy-shape misconfig before traffic shifts

## Why

`AGORA_CMS_BASE_URL` was missing on prod cmsApp env after a recent
deploy. The container booted, `/healthz` and `/healthz/system` both
returned green, and the misconfig only surfaced when the first user
clicked **Build** — at which point `/api/imager/build` returned 503
and stayed broken until PR #525 admin-merged the bicep fix.

Two reasons nothing caught it:

1. `/healthz/system` only checks db / mcp / smtp — not the
   "required-for-this-deployment-shape" pydantic settings that
   specific code paths consume at request time.
2. (Out of scope here, see follow-up PR-B.) Container Apps revision
   mode is `Single`, so even if the post-deploy probe failed, traffic
   was already on the bad revision.

This PR closes gap (1) cheaply.

## What

- **`cms/deploy_config.py`** *(new)* — small registry of
  `DeployConfigCheck`s with `(setting, env_var, required_when,
  validate, missing_message)`. Today it has one entry (`base_url`);
  adding the next required-for-shape setting is a one-liner. Mirrors
  the existing `cms/security.py` pattern intentionally.

- **`cms/main.py` lifespan** — calls
  `warn_on_missing_deploy_config(settings, logger)` next to the
  existing `warn_on_default_secrets` call. Logs a single loud
  `ERROR deploy-config:` line per finding so it shows up immediately
  in `az containerapp logs show` after deploy, not when a user
  happens to click Build.

- **`cms/main.py` `/healthz/system`** — adds a `config:` subsystem
  block (`{ok, missing: [{setting, env_var, message}]}`) and degrades
  the overall `status` if any required-for-shape setting is missing
  or invalid.

- **`.github/workflows/publish-image.yml`** post-deploy smoke probe —
  on `status != "ok"`, prints which subsystem(s) caused the
  degradation (db / mcp / each missing config var with its message),
  so the operator doesn't have to dig through container logs to find
  out *what* is degraded.

- **`tests/test_deploy_config.py`** *(new)* — 12 cases covering the
  registry: missing/blank/invalid scheme/missing host/path-rejected,
  trailing-slash and ports accepted, missing-attr tolerance, and the
  ERROR-log-emission contract.

## What this would have caught

The original `AGORA_CMS_BASE_URL`-missing deploy:
`/healthz/system` would have returned `status: "degraded"` with
`config.missing[0].env_var = "AGORA_CMS_BASE_URL"`. The smoke probe
in `publish-image.yml` already fails the `verify` job on
`status != "ok"`, so the workflow would have failed and the version
on `main` would not have bumped — paging the operator instead of
breaking prod.

## Out of scope (follow-up PR-B)

Even with this PR, `Single` revision mode means a failed verify
doesn't roll back — the bad revision is already serving 100% traffic
by the time `verify` runs. PR-B switches to `Multiple` mode +
per-revision smoke probes so traffic doesn't shift until smoke
passes.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_deploy_config.py` — 12 passed.
- `pytest tests/test_security_defaults.py` — 8 passed (no regression
  in the sibling pattern).
- `python -c "from cms.main import app"` — module imports clean.

author: carlos-alm
body:
## Summary

- `detect_removed_files` now filters out files outside Rust's supported-extension set before flagging them as removed. Files whose extension is unknown to `LanguageKind::from_extension` and absent from `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` (e.g. `.clj`, `.gleam`, `.jl`, `.fs`) are owned by the JS-side WASM backfill (#967, #1068) — the orchestrator must leave their rows alone.
- Adds `is_supported_extension` to `file_collector`, exposing the same OR predicate used by `collect_files`. `change_detection` reuses it so the two stages can never drift.
- Adds a regression unit test covering the four common WASM-only extensions.

Refs #1066.

## Why this fixes the 1-file rebuild ~2s floor

Issue #1066 has two halves. PR #1069 closed the no-op half by ensuring `file_hashes` rows are persisted for every collected file. The 1-file half remained — fast-skip can't fire when there's a real change, so each rebuild went through `tryNativeOrchestrator`, which:

1. Ran Rust's narrower `file_collector::collect_files`. WASM-only files (.clj/.gleam/.jl/.fs) were absent from `current`.
2. `detect_removed_files` flagged every such row as removed.
3. `purge_changed_files` ran `DELETE FROM nodes WHERE file = ?1` and `DELETE FROM file_hashes WHERE file = ?1` for each (`native_db.rs:1322`).
4. `backfillNativeDroppedFiles` (now on every pass per #1069) re-parsed the WASM-only files and re-inserted the rows.

On the codegraph repo, that loop hits the multi-language fixtures in `tests/benchmarks/resolution/fixtures/`, which is exactly the ~2s floor reported by the regression guard:

```
1-file rebuild: 78 → 1986 (+2446%)
```

With this change, those rows persist across incremental rebuilds and the missing-file early-return in `backfillNativeDroppedFiles` (`pipeline.ts:811`) finally fires.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI regression-guard gate shows native 1-file rebuild back under 100ms (was 1986ms in run 25415028370)
- [ ] CI regression-guard gate shows native no-op rebuild back under 30ms (was 21ms post-#1069 — not blocking but should also benefit)
- [ ] Existing `detect_removed_finds_missing` test still passes
- [ ] New `detect_removed_skips_unsupported_extensions` test passes (covers .clj/.gleam/.jl/.fs)
- [ ] No build-parity regression (the `.clj` etc. paths are still owned by the JS backfill, untouched here)

## Notes

- Verification was limited to `cargo check -p codegraph-core --lib -j 1` locally; full `cargo test` could not run on the maintainer's Windows machine due to a rustc/LLVM toolchain memory issue (unrelated to these changes). CI runs the suite.
- The `is_supported_extension` helper deliberately mirrors the OR predicate at `file_collector.rs:248-256`. Keeping it as a single function lets both stages stay in lockstep — one source of truth for what the orchestrator considers "in scope".

author: toddhal
body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for managing cleaning checklists for multiple houses. Each house has its own task list, progress state, and notification history, while maintaining a shared admin interface and unified session history.

## Key Changes

### New Data Structure
- **`src/data/houses.js`**: Central registry of houses with metadata (id, label, emoji, tasks, intro note)
- **`src/data/ethansTasks.js`**: Complete task list for Ethan's house (204 items, same structure as defaultTasks)

### Per-House State Management
- All localStorage keys are now scoped by `houseId` (e.g., `tasks_home`, `checklist_state_ethan`, `notify_fired_home`)
- `useChecklist()` hook now accepts `houseId` parameter and reloads state when house changes
- Notification system (`notifications.js`) tracks start/done events per house while maintaining a shared history with house labels

### UI Components
- **`HouseSelector.jsx`**: New pill-style toggle component for switching between houses
- Integrated into both `CleanerView` and `AdminTasks` pages
- Switching houses preserves progress (doesn't reset) and reloads from that house's localStorage keys

### Admin Interface Updates
- Admin task editor can now switch between houses and edit each house's task list independently
- Unsaved changes warning when switching houses
- Reset defaults now scoped to the active house
- Authentication refactored to use token-based system via Netlify function

### Notification & Security
- **`netlify/functions/verifyAdmin.js`**: New server-side password verification endpoint that returns a token
- **`netlify/functions/sendSms.js`**: Added validation to check app secret and whitelist destination phone
- SMS notifications now include house label in the message
- Admin login (`AdminLogin.jsx`) now calls the verification endpoint instead of client-side password check

### Environment Configuration
- Updated `.env.example` to reflect server-side auth (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `APP_SECRET`)
- Added `VITE_APP_SECRET` for client-side SMS endpoint validation
- Added `ADMIN_PHONE` for server-side SMS destination whitelist

### Other Updates
- `DoneView` now reads active house from localStorage to match the completed house
- `AdminHistory` displays house label for each session entry
- All auth checks updated to use `adminToken` instead of `isAdminAuth` flag

## Implementation Details
- House switching is non-destructive: progress is preserved in localStorage under the new house's keys
- The shared history (`checklist:history`) includes a `house` field so the admin can see which house each session belonged to
- Optional task sections (e.g., "Extra") don't count toward completion percentage
- Cross-tab sync still works: storage events trigger reloads for the active house's keys

## Summary
- Fix lightbox showing stories in wrong aspect ratio (squashed feed format).
- Prisma relation is \`Template\` (capital T); accessing \`generation.template\` was always \`undefined\`, causing dimensions to fall back to \`1080x1080\` for ALL creatives.

## Root cause
[\`prisma/schema.prisma\`](prisma/schema.prisma) declares the relation as \`Template Template @relation(...)\`. The API endpoint returns \`generation.Template\` accordingly, but [\`src/components/projects/creatives-gallery.tsx\`](src/components/projects/creatives-gallery.tsx) accessed \`generation.template\` (lowercase) in 8 places. Result: dimensions always defaulted to \`1080x1080\`, so PhotoSwipe opened stories with square aspect ratio.

The bug was masked when the secondary \`new Image()\` finished loading and updated \`imageDimensions\` with naturalWidth/naturalHeight before the user clicked. After cache-busts (e.g. fresh deploy), the click happens during the load window more often.
